prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Green Party Manifesto 2024 (policy measures only)

Health and care
- NHS: Reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access (same day if urgent); universal NHS dentistry via a new contract; invest £8bn extra in year one rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; £20bn capital for hospital building/repair over the parliament. Primary care: +£1.5bn/year by 2030; £2bn capital. Public health: restore 2015/16 budgets (+£1.5bn). Dentistry: investment rising to £3bn/year by 2030. Mental health: access to evidence-based therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school and sixth form. Cancer: prevention, earlier diagnosis (75% stage 1–2 by 2028), publicly funded research delivery. Assisted dying with safeguards. End new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year investment; national pay and career structure; protections for overseas workers; “Gloria’s Law” for care supporters. Disabled people: +5% disability benefits; oppose PIP voucher plans; free transport for 16–18 SEND pupils; workplace support. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; guaranteed counselling; extend “staying put” to 21.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; empower rent controls; end no-fault evictions; Private Residential Tenancy Boards. Retrofit: £29bn for home insulation to EPC B, £4bn for public buildings, £9bn for low‑carbon heating, £7bn for overheating adaptation (first five years). New builds: Passivhaus-equivalent; solar and low‑carbon heating; whole‑life carbon assessments; demolition needs consent; maximise material reuse. Bring empty homes into use; first-refusal powers for social landlords on certain properties.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/tCO2e rising to £500 within 10 years. Wind to ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end barriers to onshore wind; expand grid, interconnectors, storage; support green hydrogen for industry. Community energy minimum ownership; Crown Estate into public ownership; devolve Welsh assets; end imported biomass subsidies. No new nuclear; phase out existing.

Economy, taxes, and public ownership
- Green investment averaging £40bn/year (power, retrofit, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage; includes nationalisation costs for water and Big 5 retail energy). Bring rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy into public ownership. R&D: +£30bn over five years.
- Financial services: BoE mandate to support transition; fossil divestment by 2030 across banks and major non-banks; FCA to eliminate fossil listings over time.
- SMEs: regional mutual banks (£10bn capital + UKIB); grants via councils (£2bn/year); Prompt Payment Code in law.
- Welfare: +£40/week to UC/legacy; abolish five‑week wait and two‑child cap; +5% disability benefits; protect pensions with inflation and wage rises; +10% carer’s allowance; scrap bedroom tax; long‑term UBI aim.
- Tax: Wealth tax 1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings rates; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance tax; basic‑rate pension tax relief; revalue Council Tax; move toward Land Value Tax; tighten windfall taxes; VAT cuts (hospitality/arts), rises (financial services/private education); clamp down on avoidance; borrow to invest.

Nature, food, and animals
- 30% land and sea protected by 2030; Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act. Water companies to public ownership; +£1.5bn for DEFRA; soil monitoring; Right to Roam; peatland rewetting; expand woodland; £3bn/year grants for nature recovery; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Food/farming: nearly triple farm support; expand horticulture; cut pesticides; mixed farming; free school meals for all children and breakfast to Year 6; food education; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator.
- Animal protection: new Commission; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); ban snares and lead ammo; oppose badger cull.

Education
- Early years: £1.4bn/year for Sure Start; extend funded childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months (sector‑negotiated). Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/year for safe buildings/RAAC; broader curriculum incl. Natural History GCSE; academies into LA control; VAT and removal of charitable status for private schools (SEND exempt). SEND: +£5bn; universal school nurses and counsellors. FE/skills: +£12bn; sixth form +£3bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Transport
- Public transport subsidies to £10bn/year; +£19bn/5 years for PT, rail electrification, active travel; rail nationalisation; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycleways/footpaths. Oppose new road building; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; EV scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2027; end use by 2035; default 20mph; shift freight to rail. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights <3h rail; apply carbon tax to kerosene; no airport expansion; worker transition support.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, justice, foreign policy
- Fair Politics Act: repeal voter ID; proportional representation; stronger Electoral Commission; party funding reform; lobbying and think‑tank transparency; votes at 16; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; Constitutional Commission. Human rights: protect HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; repeal protest‑restricting laws; support self‑ID and “X” passports.
- Migration: safe routes; fast/fair asylum; right to work while waiting; end hostile environment, NRPF, and 10‑year route; new Department of Migration; simplify visas/fees at cost; NHS access; family reunion; voting rights for visa holders.
- Culture/media/digital: +£5bn over 5 years for local arts/sport; VAT exemption for cultural events; media ownership cap (20% market); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation; protect creators’ IP.
- Policing/justice: end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; diversion for low‑level offences; decriminalise sex work; misogyny a hate crime; +£11bn MoJ over parliament; decriminalise personal drug possession; national drugs commission.
- Foreign policy: support Ukraine; pursue EU re‑entry (customs union first, restore free movement, rejoin Erasmus); aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; end investor‑state dispute systems; cease UK arms exports to Israel; immediate Israel–Gaza ceasefire; recognise Palestine; sign TPNW, cancel Trident; remain in NATO while advocating reforms (e.g., No First Use).
